alternative: Use the GC for memory and release external resources deterministically: the block form of the acquiring method (File.open { }, Tempfile.create { }) or an explicit close in an ensure clause; model non-owning edges with ObjectSpace::WeakMap/WeakKeyMap and treat ObjectSpace.define_finalizer as an MRI-specific last resort, never as the release contract.
idiom_name: none - GC owns memory; ensure/blocks release resources; ObjectSpace::WeakMap for non-owning edges
implementation_notes: Ruby objects are managed by a tracing GC and carry no ownership information, so the classic structure has nothing deterministic to attach to. MRI exposes ObjectSpace.define_finalizer, but the documentation positions ObjectSpace as an MRI-level facility ('you should not use this library if you do not know about the MRI implementation') and finalizers run at an unspecified GC point. What replaces it: explicit close methods called from ensure, which runs on exceptions and early returns alike; the block form of stdlib acquiring methods - File.open(path) { |f| ... }, IO.pipe, Tempfile.create - where the method itself guarantees release; and ObjectSpace::WeakMap/WeakKeyMap for caches and back-references that must not keep their targets alive. Hand-written counts are meaningless under a tracing collector.
code_sketch:
class Session
  def initialize(conn) = (@conn, @open = conn, true)
  def close = @open ? (@open = false; @conn.close) : nil   # idempotent
end
def handle
  s = Session.new(connect)
  s.round_trip
ensure
  s.close                                 # runs on every exit path
end
cache = ObjectSpace::WeakMap.new          # entry dies with its key
cache[s] = Expensive.new
pitfalls: An exception raised inside ensure replaces the original one; rescue around a release that can raise.
WeakMap entries disappear without notice, so values read back must be nil-checked and re-acquired, and keys must still be live objects.
ObjectSpace.define_finalizer is GC-timed and MRI-specific (JRuby and TruffleRuby differ), and the callback receives only the object id, not the object, so it cannot implement a release contract.
Finalizers are not run for objects still alive at process exit: anything that must be flushed needs an explicit close or an at_exit hook.
